themes.name: Competency Development in Education for Sustainable Development
themes.definition: Focus on fostering specific competencies such as critical thinking, problem-solving, interdisciplinary thinking, and social skills through ESD initiatives in higher education.
evidence: [de Lea_2021] social learning indicators (learning, critical thinking, problem solving and dealing with conflict) emerged

[SieThe_2020] students perceived the simulation as a very productive tool to develop multiple learning outcomes. They considered it particularly useful with regard to improving their knowledge acquisition, problem solving, critical thinking and interpersonal skills.

[HamWhi_2023] the competencies “Interconnected, foresighted, and thinking approaches in system-dynamic contexts” and “Recognizing on one’s own perspective on a situation and problem, empathizing with other perspectives, and taking these into account when solving problems” are the most important.

themes.name: Experiential and Participatory Learning in ESD
themes.definition: Use of hands-on, engaging methods such as participatory approaches, experiential learning, simulations, and role-play to facilitate ESD in higher education.

data.meta_observations: The abstracts frequently employ case study methodologies, with a strong emphasis on qualitative and mixed-methods approaches. There is a notable focus on specific competencies and learning outcomes, often linked to Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Many studies highlight the importance of stakeholder engagement, particularly from students and educators, in refining ESD practices. Unexpected patterns include the widespread use of technology-enhanced learning despite varying regional contexts.
data.grounding_notes: Some abstracts have quality notes indicating missing elements (e.g., missing objectives, results, conclusions), so evidence extraction is limited to explicitly stated text. Quotes are verbatim from the abstracts, but in cases where quality notes mention no_quantitative_data or other issues, inferences are avoided. All article keys are from the provided closed set, and no external frameworks are imposed.
